questions.text: When I recognize that someone could be seriously hurt, preventing that harm rarely matters to me.
I notice expired items when I happen to come across them, not on a set schedule.
I make a point of having the last say before a group commits to a course of action.
I experience the end of a meaningful period — a trip, a project, a visit — with quiet acceptance rather than anguish.
I feel most purposeful when I am tutoring, coaching, or guiding someone through a challenge.
I tend to spend my weekends doing things for other people rather than pursuing my own hobbies.
I tend to pick the option that strengthens my personal position, even when alternatives would benefit the group more.
I often reshape a project's scope based on my own assessment of what matters.
I can read the atmosphere of a meeting within seconds of walking in.
I experience the buildup to an important event as a nearly unbearable crescendo of feeling.
I find it genuinely easier to give than to receive.
I do not usually notice when someone answers a question for another person to control the narrative.
I sense when a person is choosing to sit in a specific seat because of who is already sitting where.
I usually do not notice when someone adjusts their behavior after getting a social signal from someone else.
I prepare agendas before any meeting I'm responsible for.
As I consider evidence about someone's circumstances, the suffering involved has real weight for me.
I have a strong desire to leave my mark on the things I work on.
I trust that the group will find its way forward without one person driving.
I find that I cannot simply turn off my concern for someone once I have seen their pain.
I find it hard to be around conflict because my body reacts so strongly to tension.
My internal state resembles a deep, slow river — there is movement, but it is steady and unhurried.
I notice the way people edit their stories in real time based on the reactions they are getting.
I tend to miss the way people calibrate how much personal information to share based on their read of the room.
I feel uncomfortable starting a project without a clear outline of the steps involved.
Hearing that someone is going through a hard time rarely changes how I think about my own day.
When I hear unexpected good news, the rush of feeling is so strong I sometimes have to sit down.
I rarely feel the need to decompress emotionally after social interactions.
When someone I love is going through something painful, I feel little wish to ease it.
I feel most in my element when the go or no-go call is a genuine group decision.
Another person's pain matters to me whether or not I feel it myself.
I believe that my most important competition is with my past self, and I intend to keep winning.
I feel that splurging on a personal passion project is money well spent.
I share information as I learn it, refining my understanding in conversation.
I take pride in the behind-the-scenes work that makes a project succeed.
I keep a log of what I accomplish each day to maintain awareness of my productivity.
When facing a decision, I often go with my first instinct rather than deliberating at length.
